derivation.corpus: 189 findings returned across 11 review rounds of one plan.
derivation.derived_from: Rounds 1-8 only (133 findings). Recall was then measured on rounds 9-11, but the author had already read those rounds, so that figure is a contaminated holdout rather than clean unseen-data recall. The out-of-distribution result is the trustworthy generalisation evidence.
derivation.holdout_recall: Rounds 9-11 held out (56 findings): one class was novel, so a rubric derived from rounds 1-8 covers 96% at class level. CONTAMINATION-LIMITED: the author had already read rounds 9-11 when writing these properties, so this is not a clean holdout and overstates its evidence. The out-of-distribution result below is the trustworthy one.
derivation.out_of_distribution_recall: 17 of 17 probe-falsified corrections map to a property. These are the honest OOD set: every one was found by executing code against a scratch fixture, none by any reviewer in 11 rounds. P2 alone accounts for 6 of 17.
derivation.weighting_note: Properties concentrate on executed-evidence and mechanism classes because 89 of 133 training findings (67%) were in those two classes, not because they are convenient to check.
derivation.gating_surface: Script-decided properties are excluded from every prompt and refused if a model returns a verdict for one.

blocks_completion: any enumerated unit failing a mandatory unit-scoped property, unless that unit carries a recorded waiver with a reason
any mandatory document-scoped existential property not satisfied
any declared probe not passing, or not reproducible from a repository-relative path
any untriaged entry from the open-ended hunt
any open finding of severity critical or high
gate.no_threshold: There is no ratio and no score. Every failing unit is individually fixed or individually waived, so the gate terminates on a finite set and names exactly what remains.
gate.never_a_gate: The replaced scalar produced mean 55.1 sd 8.1 range 38-64 across seven scorings of one byte-identical document, statistically indistinguishable from eleven rounds of real repair (mean 55.1 sd 9.3).

properties.statement: Every numeric count, file path, symbol name, and line reference in the plan is accompanied by the exact command that produced it.
properties.evidence: For each such claim, the command string and its verbatim output.
ood_catches: C4: captureRepositoryPreimage was claimed to return 4 keys; it returns 6.
properties.advisory_because: Universally quantified over an unbounded set. Measured: returns fail or unverified on every document tested, including a corrected one, so it discriminates nothing. Its named instances are still valuable and route to the hunt.

properties.statement: Every claim about library, runtime, or tool behaviour is backed by an executed command. Reading source, documentation, or --help output does not satisfy this.
properties.evidence: The command and its real output, run against a scratch fixture.
ood_catches: C3: `git rm --cached` was assumed to unstage staged content; it does not.
C5: `git commit --only` was assumed to accept a new untracked path; it exits 1.
C6: a deletion staged with `git rm` breaks the later `git add -A`.
C11: replacing an unpublished checkpoint was assumed to add a commit; it keeps the parent.
C14: a bare `update-ref` writes an unlabelled reflog entry.

properties.statement: No claim in the plan is contradicted by the output of a command the plan itself cites.
properties.evidence: Re-run each cited command; compare against the quoted output.
properties.advisory_because: Universally quantified over an unbounded set. Measured: returns fail or unverified on every document tested, including a corrected one, so it discriminates nothing. Its named instances are still valuable and route to the hunt.

properties.statement: Every mechanism the plan describes has an executable probe that runs it against a scratch fixture, and the probe's real output is quoted in the plan.
properties.evidence: Probe path, invocation, and pass count.
ood_catches: C12: committing through the caller's index was only shown wrong by running it; a private index is required.

properties.statement: Every failure and rollback path has a probe that injects the failure at that exact boundary and asserts the post-failure state.
properties.evidence: One probe per named boundary, with the asserted preimage.
ood_catches: C7: entry restoration was mistaken for preimage restoration.
C15: the amend tree seed was HEAD^, silently dropping implementation files.

properties.statement: Every concurrency, ordering, or interleaving hazard named in the plan has a probe reproducing the hazardous interleaving, and that probe fails when the guard is removed.
properties.evidence: The probe, and its failure with the guard removed.
ood_catches: C2: the snapshot boundary is the transaction, not the commit.
C9: the snapshot must be taken inside the lock.
C16: `update-ref` without its expected-old argument silently loses a concurrent commit.

properties.statement: Every destructive or state-mutating operation has a probe proving that state it does not own is unchanged, including state a third party mutated concurrently, and including after an injected failure.
properties.evidence: Probe asserting unowned state byte-identical after success and after failure.
ood_catches: C1: restoring owned-path bytes would have destroyed the user's own edits.
C8: a raw index write is repository-wide and reverts a third party's staged work.
C15: the amend seed dropped files the implementation checkpoint had introduced.

properties.statement: Every acceptance row states the exact observable that distinguishes pass from fail: either a specific exit status, or a literal substring of the command output. "The command succeeds" or "the check passes" does not satisfy this; the discriminating token must be written down.
properties.evidence: Per row: the exit status or the literal output substring, quoted verbatim.
properties.rewritten_because: The original wording mixed a structural check with a judgement and returned pass in 4 of 7 fresh contexts on identical bytes - a coin flip on a mandatory gate. The structural half is now script-checked.

properties.statement: Every acceptance row states a mutation to the implementation that makes it fail, and that mutation has been performed and observed to fail.
properties.evidence: The named mutation and the observed failure output.

properties.statement: At least one acceptance row exercises a complete success path end to end, so the suite cannot pass by refusing everything.
properties.evidence: The row, and its command's success output.

properties.statement: Every value the plan writes into a closed set defined elsewhere in the repository is a member of that set as the source defines it today.
properties.evidence: The source file and line defining the set, and the plan's values.
ood_catches: C10: the implementation checkpoint was required to change the record; the contract commits implementation first.

properties.statement: Every validator, reducer, or helper the plan relies on is named with its file and the specific invariant it enforces, and that invariant is quoted from the source.
properties.evidence: File, symbol, and the quoted invariant.
ood_catches: C4: the preimage helper's real key set was never quoted.
C17: the plan lock and the repository lock are different locks with different scopes.

properties.statement: The declared affected paths exactly match the set of paths the steps modify: none modified that is undeclared, none declared that is untouched.
properties.evidence: The declared list and the per-step path list, compared.

properties.statement: The declared blast radius accounts for every synchronization or coupling rule the repository mandates for the surfaces being changed.
properties.evidence: The mandating rule, quoted with its path, and where the plan satisfies it.

properties.statement: No two passages of the plan state incompatible requirements, and no superseded text remains anywhere in the document.
properties.evidence: The passage pairs checked, and the absence of correction or changelog narrative.
properties.advisory_because: Universally quantified over an unbounded set. Measured: returns fail or unverified on every document tested, including a corrected one, so it discriminates nothing. Its named instances are still valuable and route to the hunt.

properties.statement: Every step's stated dependencies are satisfiable in the stated order, and no step's done-condition depends on work a later step performs.
properties.evidence: The dependency graph and a valid topological order.

properties.statement: Every command a cold implementer must run is given exactly, including working directory and required environment, with nothing left to infer.
properties.evidence: The commands, run from a clean shell.

properties.statement: The plan states, for each step, what observable proves it done, without reference to a score or a reviewer's opinion.
properties.optional_because: Useful but not load-bearing: a step whose observable is implied by its acceptance rows is still executable.

properties.statement: At least one mechanism is declared with a {mechanism} marker, or a waiver records that this plan builds and relies on none.
properties.evidence: The declared mechanism headings, enumerated by script.
properties.exists_because: The {mechanism} marker is opt-in, so a plan declaring nothing would give the five probe properties an empty set to quantify over and they would all pass vacuously - the acceptance-vacuous class from this rubric's own source corpus. Script-checked, so it costs no variance.

open_hunt.budget: one pass per round, fresh context, rubric NOT supplied
open_hunt.purpose: Recall must not be capped by this rubric, which its own author wrote. A hunt finding matching no property is a rubric hole and is recorded as a proposed property.
open_hunt.blocks_completion_when: any hunt finding is untriaged, or a triaged critical or high finding is unresolved
open_hunt.promotion_to_mandatory: Requires explicit human ratification. Neither the plan author nor the judging model may promote a property to mandatory.

post_implementation_review.rationale: Of 133 training findings, 89 (67%) were wrong-mechanism or unbacked-claim, and 17 of 17 probe-falsified corrections came from executing code rather than from any review. Review is most valuable pointed at running code.
triggers: a probe result contradicts the plan text
the implementer declares uncertainty about a mechanism
the next action crosses an irreversible boundary: push, release, deploy, or production access
post_implementation_review.caveat: The plan's own acceptance gates may encode the same misconception the plan does, so a post-implementation review must probe destructive transitions, rollback, and negative cases in isolation rather than relying on the suite passing.

stability_requirement.why: The measured failure of the previous design was variance on identical input, not poor coverage. A vector gate inherits that defect unless its verdicts are stable.
stability_requirement.test: Dispatch the identical plan bundle to 7 fresh contexts with this rubric and compare per-property verdicts.
stability_requirement.threshold: At least 6 of 7 verdicts identical for every mandatory property. A property that cannot be judged reproducibly is not a gate; it is rewritten or demoted.

measured.fixture: round-7 sealed bundle, 31,037 bytes, the last written before any probe existed
measured.binary_gate_agreement: 16 of 17 mandatory properties identical in 7 of 7 runs
measured.reason_axis_note: P5 and P6 split between fail and unverified while agreeing 7/7 on blocking, so stability is measured on the bit the gate consumes.
measured.validity: P2, P4, P5, P6, P7 refused the pre-probe bundle in 7 of 7 runs - the five properties claimed to catch the 17 corrections only executing code ever found.
measured.comparison: The replaced scalar produced sd 8.1 and a 26-point range on one byte-identical document.

specificity.test: the corrected round-11 bundle, which quotes 33 of 33 passing probes, judged by 3 fresh contexts
specificity.result: 0 of 14 previously-blocking document-level properties cleared. The gate never opened, which is why unit scoping replaced document scoping.
specificity.legitimate_failures_found: P4 and P17 correctly refused because the probe suite lives at an operator-local path outside the repository, so a cold implementer cannot reproduce the plan's strongest evidence. That defect is real and was not visible to eleven rounds of prose review.
specificity.unit_agreement: Where replicates named concrete units they agreed far better than on the document boolean: P9 named exactly {A22, A25, A27} in 3 of 3 contexts; P6, P9 and P10 reached full consensus in the 7-context run. The two worst (P8 25%, P16 29%) were the properties whose unit boundaries were undefined, which is why unit sets are now enumerated by script.

unit_sets._why: Gating requires a finite, script-enumerable denominator. A property universally quantified over an unbounded set - "every numeric claim in a 40KB document" - failed in 7 of 7 fresh contexts on both a known-bad and a corrected bundle, because at least one instance always violates it. Such properties cannot gate; they advise.
unit_sets.acceptance_rows: Rows of the Acceptance criteria table, keyed by their declared id.
unit_sets.steps_rows: Rows of the Steps table, keyed by step number.
unit_sets.named_mechanisms: Each mechanism the plan builds or relies on, DECLARED by appending {mechanism} to its heading. Explicit rather than inferred: inference mis-enumerated 3 of 5 headings in a real plan and would have demanded executable probes for a facts table and a path list.

scoping_rule.universal over an unbounded set: advisory only - feeds the open hunt, never blocks
scoping_rule.existential: gates at document level, because a single witness satisfies it

cli.never: No subcommand computes, prints, or accepts a score.

subcommands.units: enumerate the bounded unit sets; deterministic, no model involved
subcommands.sections: section id -> digest map, derived from the document headings
subcommands.prompt: build the review prompt: rubric plus enumerated units, or --hunt for a bare no-rubric pass
subcommands.validate: refuse an incoherent return before it can be acted on
subcommands.ledger: merge a return into the persistent finding ledger
subcommands.waive: record a waiver for one failing unit, with a reason and an acceptor
subcommands.gate: report CLEAR or BLOCKED and exactly what remains
subcommands.apply: apply byte-exact fixes in the stated order; dry run unless --commit
subcommands.check: run the deterministic script-checked properties; no model involved

cli.not: This is NOT the canonical plan-review path. `plan-reviewer` owns PlanReviewV1 evidence, its own verdict vocabulary (pass|repair|blocked), immutable bundle identity, and the per-phase review permits. This tool is an authoring-time self-check whose verdicts are never review evidence.
